producer_report.summary: The drain's closing summary now covers the whole run across rebuild re-execs. A new `drain::run_pass` wraps one pass. Before the re-exec it writes the run's tallies so far to `drain.carry` in the state directory: landed, spend, job lines (which are the jobs started), notes, rebases, improvement turns, the rating and held_back. The continuing process takes that file and adds it to its own Report. The restart limits are computed inside `drain()` before the merge, so the remaining budget and job limit are unchanged and spend is not double-counted. The report's `budget_usd` becomes the whole run's, so the summary reads `spent X of Y` with X no larger than Y. `guarded` removes a carry when the start is not the drain's own exec, so a fresh drain starts at zero. An unreadable carry is ignored, and a failed exec clears the file. Plan, queue and waiting lists stay those of the last pass. The `drain` command in commands.rs now calls `run_pass` in place of the bare `follow_restart`. I added four tests in tests/drain.rs, updated the module docs, and added a CHANGELOG entry. The new tests pass. fmt, clippy -D warnings and `cargo test --locked` passed in my runs, but I did not run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` on its own. I ran the full suite once, and that suite includes the policy test.

checks_run.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain -- a_rebuild_between a_fresh_drain the_restart_limits a_failed_exec

checks_run.note: Every result line ok, 0 failed. The whole suite includes tests/drain.rs (194 passed), the policy scan and the mirrors test. I read only the quiet output and did not inspect those two individually.

criteria_check.criterion: A drain test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or unit tests in drain.rs) runs a first pass that lands one job and ends Stop::Rebuilt, then a continuing pass that lands a second job, and asserts the final report has landed == 2, spent_usd equal to the sum of both passes' spend, and both jobs in jobs. Check by running `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
criteria_check.evidence: The test `a_rebuild_between_two_landings_reports_the_whole_run` in tests/drain.rs passed. It runs `whole_run`, which wraps `run_pass` around `drain::drain` over the rebuilding Stub, with the exec stood in for by a closure that runs the next pass. The first pass ends Stop::Rebuilt. It asserts `rebuilds == 1`, landed == 2, jobs items [a, b], and spent_usd ≈ 1.6 (0.8 per pass). It also asserts `drain.carry` exists while the restart closure runs and is gone afterwards. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain -- a_rebuild_between a_fresh_drain the_restart_limits a_failed_exec`: 4 passed.

criteria_check.criterion: The rendered closing summary (display::drain) for that continued run shows both landings and the whole-run spend, not just the last pass. The test asserts on the printed text.
criteria_check.evidence:
The same test asserts the `display::drain(&report)` text contains `landed      2
`, does not contain `landed      1
`, contains `(item a)` and `(item b)`, and contains `spent       $1.60 of $9.00
`. It also checks the JSON value (landed 2, two jobs). It passed.

criteria_check.criterion: A fresh drain with no carry from a rebuild still reports only its own tallies (landed 0 starts at 0), and a stale carry is not applied to it. A test covers it; run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
criteria_check.evidence: The test `a_fresh_drain_and_a_stale_carry_start_at_zero` drives `drain::guarded` with `RealProcs` in a tempdir. (a) With no carry the report has landed 1, one job line, and spend below 1.0. (b) A stale carry from `store_carry` with a fresh start is dropped: landed 1, one job line, budget 9.0, file gone. (c) When the pid file names this process, the carry is applied: landed 4, items [x, y, z, a], spent 7.8, file gone. (d) The file contents `not json` count as no carry: landed 1, file removed. `a_failed_exec_leaves_no_carry_behind` also passed. Both ran and passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Jobs started, per-item outcomes (JobLine entries) and spend are all carried, and the remaining budget and job limit passed to the continuing pass are unchanged, so spend is not double-counted against the budget. A test asserts budget_usd and max_jobs in the restart.
criteria_check.evidence: The test `the_restart_limits_are_unchanged_and_spend_is_carried_once_across_two_rebuilds` runs three passes over items a, b, c with two rebuilds. It records every `Limits` passed to the restart closure. The first is budget 8.2, max_jobs 9, target 4; the second is budget 7.4, max_jobs 8. These match the existing single-pass values. The final report has landed 3, jobs [a, b, c] (jobs started = 3), spent ≈ 2.4 (counted once), budget 9.0 and outcome_changed true. It passed.

open_issues: The real exec is not exercised in tests: they stand in for it with a closure that calls `run_pass` again. The carry still goes through the real file. The only new behaviour at the exec boundary is a file write and read.

The per-pass 'rebases: x of y' note is carried as written, so a continued run's notes list can show each pass's note next to the summed `rebases` tally. Improvement turns keep the dispatch number each pass counted.
mistakes: I did not run the new tests against the pre-change source to show they fail without it. The assertions would fail by construction if the merge were absent.
learnings: `PidGuard::acquire` returns `carried_over == true` exactly when the pid file names this process, which is what an exec produces. That makes it a precise signal for whether a carry is owned.
`Restart` is computed inside `drain()` from the pass's own State, so merging tallies after `drain()` returns leaves the remaining budget and job limit untouched.
The Stub in tests/drain.rs pays 0.8 per item (read 0.1, run 0.5, rate 0.2), and `unrelated` items touch crates/, which triggers a rebuild.
desires: A way to read a saved tool-output file: the harness persisted a large cargo test log outside the working directory, and the policy hook blocked reading it, so I had to rerun the suite in quiet mode.
